processing_steps.duration: about 12 h (crystal growth with subsequent cooling)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Monocrystals with up to 10 cm length grown by the Bridgman method; the alloy is the Fe-16%Al monocrystal (real Al 16.0 at.% / 8.4 wt.-%, C 45 wt.ppm, Si 40 wt.ppm, O 60).
At 1100 °C the specimens were heat-treated usually only 15 min; for all heat treatments above 300 °C the specimens were enclosed in evacuated (10^-6 bar) SiO2 capsules.
Interrupted furnace cooling (1100 °C FC 600 °C) leaving the specimen at 600 °C, chosen to reach minimum short-range ordering without a direct high-temperature quench.
Subsequent water quench from 600 °C, completing the '1100 °C FC 600 °C Q' state; quenching from 600 °C suppresses short-range ordering nearly completely.

structures.overall_structure: Fe-16%Al monocrystal (single crystal) in the state produced by 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q, i.e. with minimum short-range ordering. Hardness specimens were (111)-oriented; compression specimens were [112]-oriented.

phases_present.phase_name: Fe-16 at.%Al solid solution (bcc, minimum short-range order)

inclusions: rare globular AlN inclusions with diameters up to 30 µm (identified by EDX)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: prior heat treatment: 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q (furnace cooling from 1100 °C down to 600 °C with subsequent water quench); HU reported as average of more than 40 measurements
compression test; 0.2% proof stress definition; prior heat treatment: 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Compressive stress-strain curve for [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal after 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q (RT, 10^-4 s^-1): rises steeply through a knee at roughly 1.5–2% strain, then a nearly flat plateau with only slight hardening out to ~5.5% strain, plateauing near the 430–440 MPa level (lowest group, together with 'as grown').

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Fischerscope H100 (max load 1 N); HU = F/(26.43·h²) [N/mm²]
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; more than 40 measurements averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the effect of prior heat treatment (state of atomic order) on the hardness of the (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q condition yields HU ~2000 N/mm², equal to the as-grown monocrystal; heat treatment shifts HU by only about 5–10% around 2000 N/mm².

characterization_methods.technique: Uniaxial compression testing (0.2% proof stress; total straining at least 5%)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; strain rate 10^-4 s^-1; specimens 5×5×10 mm³, monocrystals polished with 3 µm diamond paste before testing
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the compressive stress-strain behaviour / yield stress of the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal after prior heat treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q curve is essentially the same as as-grown and furnace-cooled (to RT) material; only quench from 1100 °C + 300 °C/14 d anneal gives a higher yield stress.

characterization_methods.technique: Optical microscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy-dispersive X-ray analysis (EDX)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Specimens etched with alcoholic 10% nitric acid for optical microscopy; SEM for fracture surfaces and qualitative precipitate analysis
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain boundaries/precipitates (optical) and study fracture surfaces and identify particles such as AlN inclusions (SEM/EDX)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Monocrystals contain rare globular AlN inclusions (up to 30 µm) identified by EDX.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Philips CM20 instrument, 200 kV; thin foils prepared by electrolytic twin-jet polishing at -30 °C, 12 V, 7:3 methanol:nitric acid, plus ion milling if needed
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to compare quenched vs furnace-cooled deformation substructures in Fe-Al alloys (reported for Fe-12%Al and for polycrystalline Fe-16%Al).

unmapped_findings: The 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q condition was designed to reach minimum short-range ordering: quenching from 600 °C suppresses short-range ordering nearly completely, whereas maximum ordering requires a 250 °C/14 day anneal; nevertheless this minimum-order state gave the same hardness as the as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal (HU ~2000 N/mm²), so short-range order has no major impact on hardness.

For the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal the 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q compressive stress-strain curve (RT, 10^-4 s^-1) is essentially identical to the as-grown and furnace-cooled (to RT) curves; only quenching from 1100 °C followed by a 300 °C/14 day anneal produced a higher yield stress, i.e. only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour.

In Fig. 1 this condition is labelled '1100°C FC600°CQ' (furnace cooling from 1100 °C down to 600 °C with subsequent water quench) and is also written as '1100 °C FC 600 °CQ'; no numeric HU value is printed in the figure, so ~2000 N/mm² is read against the 2000 N/mm² gridline.
